page.overview:
Who is Bast?

Bast, also known as Bubastis, is a goddess from Egyptian mythology, incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by Robert Bloch's short story "The Suicide in the Study".

Another spelling of her name is Bastet, but due to the way the Egyptian language works, it does not change the pronunciation. The additional 'et' ending is added merely to emphasize the t in her name which denotes that she is female.

Bast is the Egyptian goddess of cats and in legend the daughter of Isis. (: "The Brood of Bubastis") She is an Elder God and the queen of all cats on Earth. However, her authority does not extend to the cats of Saturn and Uranus. The cats of these planets are associated with different deities. (: Malleus Monstrorum)

Bast is also linked with ghouls by some Saracen sorcerers, who call her "the Chewer of Corpses". A ghoul-cult to Bast fled from the Middle East to Cornwall, where they established a secret temple. (: "The Brood of Bubastis") It is believed that this was orchestrated by Nephren-Ka and that a false doctrine was spread to revive the worship of Nyarlathotep. (: Cathulhu)
